title: Creative Director (m/w/d)
description_clean:
Jobbeschreibung
Über Teaching Socials
Teaching Socials ist die führende Unternehmensberatung für Personal Brands im Finanz- & Immobilienbereich im DACH-Raum. Unser Team aus 25 High-Performern hat innerhalb von 2 Jahren ein konstantes Monatswachstum von über 750.000 € aufgebaut. Wir verbinden Sichtbarkeit, Kundenakquise und Unternehmenswachstum in einem System – und du sorgst mit deinen Videos dafür, dass aus Ideen Reichweite, aus Zuschauern qualifizierte Leads und aus Personal Brands messbare Ergebnisse werden.
Deine Aufgaben
Content-Strategie: Du entwickelst für jeden Kunden einen Content-Plan für die nächsten Wochen und leitest daraus einen klaren Produktionsplan für die Cutter ab.

Ideen und Skripte: Du findest die Themen, Hooks und Titel für alle Hauptvideos auf YouTube und schreibst die Skripte selbst.
Dreh: Du begleitest Drehs, verstehst Kamera, Licht und Ton und greifst selbst zur Kamera, wenn es nötig ist.
Schnitt und Qualität: Du gibst jedes Video frei, bevor es zum Kunden geht. Was nicht gut genug ist, geht zurück.
Cutter-Führung: Du führst das Cutter-Team, gibst regelmäßig konkretes Feedback und machst jeden Editor messbar besser.
Shortform und Ads: Du sorgst dafür, dass aus jedem Longform-Video verwertbare Clips und Ad-Creatives entstehen.
Kundenkommunikation: Du führst die Weeklys mit unseren Kunden, erklärst, was produziert wird und warum, und vertrittst deine Entscheidungen auch dann, wenn der Kunde anders denkt.

Was für dich drin ist:

Starkes Team: Familiäres Umfeld, gemeinsame Erfolge und Geburtstage
Schnelle Wege: Deine Ideen werden intern umgesetzt, statt in endlosen Entscheidungsschleifen zu versanden
Direkter Impact: Deine Videos beeinflussen unmittelbar Reichweite, Leads und Umsätze unserer Kunden
Führung: Du führst ein eigenes Cutter-Team und prägst, wie bei uns Content entsteht
Wachstum: Du arbeitest mit unterschiedlichen Personal Brands, Formaten und Zielgruppen und entwickelst dich als Creator und Führungskraft kontinuierlich weiter

Das bringst du mit:

Nachweisbare Erfahrung als Content Creator, Video Producer oder Head of Content, idealerweise mit Fokus auf YouTube-Longform, Shortform und Video-Ads
Ein Portfolio mit Videos, die du verantwortet hast, idealerweise mit messbaren Ergebnissen wie Views, Klickrate und Zuschauerbindung
Fundiertes Verständnis dafür, was ein Video viral macht: Hook, Titel, Thumbnail, Storytelling und Retention
Starkes Gespür für Ideen und Skripte: Du schreibst YouTube-Skripte selbst, die Zuschauer bis zum Ende halten
Editing auf hohem Niveau: Longform, Shortform und cinematic – idealerweise bist du selbst Creator
Sicherer Umgang mit Kamera, Licht und Ton: Du kannst selbst drehen
Verständnis für Video-Ads und ihre Rolle im Funnel und in der Customer Journey
Sicherer Umgang mit relevanten Kennzahlen wie CTR, Zuschauerbindung, Views und CPL
Führungserfahrung: Du steuerst mehrere Cutter gleichzeitig, planst Produktion und gibst Feedback, das dein Team besser macht
Souveräne Kundenkommunikation: Du führst Weeklys und vertrittst deine Content-Entscheidungen auch gegenüber anspruchsvollen Unternehmern
Hohe Standards: Kein Video verlässt dein Team, hinter dem du nicht selbst stehst
Eigenverantwortung: Du wartest nicht auf Ansagen, sondern bringst eigene Ideen und Trends ein
Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau
Ein Plus: Erfahrung mit Podcast- und Event-Drehs sowie tiefes Technik-Verständnis (Kamera-Setups, Equipment, Workflows)

Du passt eher nicht zu uns, wenn …

du lieber schöne Bilder produzierst, statt Videos, die Reichweite und Nachfrage erzeugen
du nur schneiden willst und Ideen, Skripte und Strategie anderen überlässt
du dich auf Bauchgefühl verlässt und Klickrate, Retention und Views ignorierst
du Videos rausgibst, hinter denen du selbst nicht stehst
du Trends anderer kopierst, statt eigene Ideen und Formate zu entwickeln
du Feedback persönlich nimmst oder deinem Team kein klares Feedback geben willst
du lange an einem einzelnen Video feilst, aber Schwierigkeiten hast, im Volumen zu liefern
du Deadlines eher als Empfehlung siehst
du Kunden nicht klar sagen magst, wenn etwas nicht funktioniert
dich klare Ziele, Zahlen und ein performanceorientiertes Umfeld eher abschrecken
du einfach nur einen Job suchst und nicht bereit bist, dich fachlich und persönlich weiterzuentwickeln

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 
Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.
The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.
The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.
This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.
The mandate

 Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
 Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would. You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
 Win the right members, efficiently. You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
 Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances. Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
 Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless. You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
 Build one Customer organisation, not four. Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
 Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call. You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate
This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).

Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.
What this role is not

Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

The Generalist named us among the Future 50.The RoleThis is Dust's first PM hire. You'll work closely with the product team, turning raw GTM signal, company priorities, and user feedback into well-formed problems the team can act on.What you will change:A lot of product signal doesn't reach the team in an actionable shape today. You'll create and run the process that connects signal to shaping to prioritization.Implementing company strategies across functions requires ownership and orchestration. You'll translate company priorities into an intelligible, trackable set of product, marketing, and operations initiatives.You'll enrich prioritized projects with distilled business and user context and market perspective so that the people building them make better decisions.Our designers and engineers stay close to product decisions from conception to delivery. You enable distributed ownership, you don't replace it.What You'll DoQualify and synthesize feedback: Sit at the intersection of GTM, users, and product. Feed that back into the next round of decisions.Improve internal coordination: Connect Marketing, Comms, GTM, and Product — reduce the friction that slows things down when multiple functions need to move together.Own outcomes, not outputs: For cross-functional initiatives, you'll own the goal — objectives, KPIs, orchestration, reporting.Own artefacts in the Dust platform (agents, skills, data, etc..) to continuously rewire and augment the above for yourself and the teamWhat You Can ExpectTeamDust is a growing team of about a 100 people. We’ll look at how you gather context, identify the important problems, collaborate on possible approaches, and leave ownership with the people closest to the work.We care more about the quality of your reasoning and collaboration than about arriving at a predetermined answer.What We're Looking ForFounding PM mentality: Senior individual contributor and builder balancing capacity to build the practice in the company while being hands-on.5–8+ years of product experience, including time at an early-stage company where you had to build process from scratch.Genuine product taste. You know great from good in the world of tech products, and you bring deep perspective, judgment and conviction to any preferences you voice.Excellent information synthesis skills, distilling a messy pile of customer feedback, sales calls, and Slack threads into sharp problems.Technical proficiency earn the respect of engineers. You don't need to code, but you understand systems and tradeoffs easily deeply.Builder mindset at heart. You use AI tools fluently and you're excited about what they unlock for how PMs operate. You've thrived in environments where everyone is a builder and you want to strengthen that.Effective communication. You'd rather say one clear thing than three vague things.Comfort with distributed authority. You influence by being right, not by being in charge.LocationWe're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.Why DustThe models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist. Learn how we think and work.Our product constitution, a story about our missionYour Next Co-Worker Isn’t Human, Stanislas Polu, VivaTech 2026. title: Senior Data Scientist/ML Ops Engineer (all genders)
description_clean:
Responsibilities
With a mission to empower 15.6 million house owners across Germany and the broader DACH region, we at Aroundhome are building a platform where every strategic decision is powered by data. We’re a team of around 250 people, and to take the next step, we’re looking for an experienced and hands-on Senior Data Scientist (all genders) to bring machine learning into the heart of our product.
As a Senior Data Scientist, you will build Aroundhome’s first machine learning model in production: the logic that decides which partners each homeowner is matched with. You will start from the problems homeowners and partners actually have, and own the solution end to end, in a small new team with a product manager, an engineer and the team lead.
Responsibilities:

Start from the Customer: Understand what homeowners and partners need from a match, and turn that into the outcomes and guardrails your models optimize for, not just model metrics.
Own Our Matching Models: Build and run the models behind our partner matching, end to end: data, features, training, evaluation, deployment and monitoring.
Make Every Match Count: Improve our matching logic with deployed models that make the most efficient use of partner capacity, raise match rates, and account for regional supply and demand.
Prove Impact: Measure every improvement against our current logic in controlled experiments designed for a two-sided marketplace, before it scales.
Build the Data Foundation: Create the datasets and pipelines your models need, together with our engineer and the Data Engineering team. In the first months, this is a big part of the role.
Shape Our ML Stack: Decide with the team how and where models run, and set the practices for machine learning at Aroundhome.
Translate Models into Decisions: Explain trade-offs between customer experience, partner fulfillment and revenue to product managers, partner category managers, key account managers and senior leadership.

Skills

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree or equivalent practical experience in a quantitative field (e.g., Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics).
Proven experience (5+ years) in applied data science, including at least one ads, ranking, pricing or marketplace model you took to production.
Production-grade Python and advanced SQL, plus hands-on experience with modern data tooling (e.g., dbt, Airflow, Spark).
Experience deploying and monitoring models on a cloud ML platform (e.g., SageMaker, Vertex AI, MLflow).
Solid foundation in experiment design and causal inference, ideally in a marketplace where test and control groups affect each other.
Hands-on experience with classical machine learning (e.g., gradient-boosted trees), probability calibration and offline vs online evaluation.
A product mindset: you define success in homeowner and partner outcomes, challenge assumptions with evidence, and add complexity only where it earns its place.
Strong communication skills and the ability to explain models and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
A plus: experience with recommender systems or search ranking.

What we offer
Hybrid Work // Stay flexible: Decide freely whether you want to work from our office in Berlin, from home throughout Germany, or fully remote from Portugal. Additionally, we offer you the possibility to work up to 30 days per year from selected EU countries.  
Room to grow // Stay curious: In regular/annual feedback meetings, you design your own personal development path together with your team lead. In addition, we offer monthly Tech Talks, an annual training budget, free access to LinkedIn Learning as well as great workshops to seek new input and specific training for your personal development.  
Mental & physical health // Stay healthy & active: We care about your well-being and support your health with a discounted membership at Urban Sports Club. In addition, our cooperation partner “Fürstenberg Institute” is available to you and your family members with advice and support when it comes to mental health & coaching.  
Taking responsibility // We #care: We care for our planet and the people who are living on it. To make our world a little bit better, our ESG Team (Environmental, Social & Governance) promotes our awareness for environmentally friendly behavior. In addition, we work with JobRad, offer a discounted BVG ticket, and actively support social projects in Berlin at our annual Social Day to give something back.  
Teamspirit // Stay connected: What drives us is our sense of community. That's why we celebrate our Company Day once a month at our Potsdamer Platz office, where everyone gets together in person. In addition to a comprehensive update of our C-Board, the main focus is on togetherness and the exchange of ideas over lunch and dinner together.  Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

How fast should an LLM building block run on our hardware? How fast does it actually run, and what would make it faster?

The role
Help make the latest AI models run well on our silicon. You'll work from model code to measured hardware performance: bring up new architectures, track down accuracy failures, and improve latency, throughput, and memory use.
The bigger challenge is making that work repeatable. You'll build an agentic harness that can explore implementations, run experiments, check results, and guide the next change. Every investigation should leave behind better software, better tests, and a shorter path for the next model.
We're looking for an excellent software engineer who understands LLM inference deeply and knows how to put coding agents to work. You'll own substantial parts of our SDK and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your particular focus will be numerical optimization: finding where precision matters, where computation can be cheaper, and how to preserve model quality.
What you'll do

Build the agentic workflows. Give agents the tools to inspect models, change implementations and numerical settings, run emulation and hardware experiments, and diagnose failures. Build the feedback and evaluation that make the results trustworthy.
Bring up new models quickly; make them go brrrr. Work with engineers across the stack to take unfamiliar architectures from reference code to validated, performant execution on our accelerator. Turn what you learn into reusable model support and SDK improvements.
Optimize numerics. Explore precision, accumulation, and quantization choices across the model. Understand how they interact with kernels, KV caches, memory, and distributed execution, then measure the gains in latency, throughput, and memory use against model quality on silicon.
Make numerical quality measurable. Build conversion and emulation software that lets you test numerical choices quickly. Compare activations and outputs against reference models, trace accuracy regressions to their source, and validate changes with end-to-end model evaluations.
Ship software that lasts. Own design, implementation, testing, and delivery. Build clear APIs that are easy to use for agents. Make difficult bugs reproducible and keep them from returning. Know when to build fast, and when to build thoroughly.
Shape the next chip. Work with hardware architects to test how numerical formats and arithmetic choices affect real models. Turn those findings into better hardware and algorithm designs.

What we need from you

You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model's implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention, KV caches, MoE, batching, and parallelism. You understand how these translate into compute, memory, and communication on an accelerator.
You build excellent software. You've owned substantial systems and delivered complex features from design through production. You're strong in Python, thoughtful about interfaces, and rigorous about abstractions and testing.
You are fluent with agentic tooling. You'd rather build the agent that runs the optimization than doing it by hand; and running numerous agents in parallel excites you. You know what is required for agents to work effectively in a large software organization, and you have the judgement when an agentic loop still needs a human.
You take ownership and bring others along. You form clear hypotheses, test them, and drive problems to resolution across software boundaries. You communicate clearly through specs, design docs, and reviews that people and agents can act on. You explain complex trade-offs, give direct feedback, and make the people around you better.

If you tick a few of these boxes, we'd love to hear from you.
We'd be thrilled if you had

Expertise in improving inference systems like debugging and optimizing the runtime of complex models and reasoning about accuracy-performance trade-offs.
Experience with ML compilers, accelerator SDKs, or model compression libraries, particularly for non-NVIDIA accelerators such as TPU, Trainium/Inferentia, Tenstorrent, Groq, or Cerebras.
Experience with model quantization, sparsity, codebooks, low-rank factorization or other compression techniques.
Contributions to distributed inference or serving frameworks such as vLLM or SGLang.

Why join us
Your code will help determine how quickly we support new models, how efficiently they run, and what we build into our next chip. You'll own meaningful software, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon.
If you want to build the tools, solve the hard failures, and help set the engineering direction of a new inference platform, we'd like to hear from you.

description_clean: Contexte :ENSTA est un établissement d’enseignement supérieur et de recherche sous tutelle du ministère des Armées. Paris (https://www.hi-paris.fr/). La recherche sera menée à l'ENSTA, Institut Polytechnique de Paris. Le poste offre l'opportunité de travailler sur un sujet de recherche stimulant et impactant. Les connaissances, l'innovation et les compétences développées dans le cadre de ce poste offriront d'excellentes perspectives d'évolution de carrière tant dans l'industrie que dans le monde universitaire.Le changement climatique exige des stratégies innovantes pour exploiter les énergies renouvelables. Le sous-sol de la Terre offre un potentiel important grâce à des technologies telles que l'énergie géothermique profonde, le stockage souterrain de l'hydrogène et le captage, l'utilisation et le stockage du carbone (CCUS). Ces méthodes pourraient transformer le paysage énergétique de la France et de l'Europe, mais elles sont souvent entravées par la sismicité induite par l'injection de fluides dans la croûte terrestre.Pour relever ce défi, il faut des solutions avancées. La théorie du contrôle mathématique, telle qu'explorée dans le projet INJECT du CER (https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101087771), offre des stratégies pour minimiser les risques sismiques tout en optimisant la production d'énergie. Équiper des équipes de LLM et de coding agents prend un après-midi. Les faire travailler en AI-Native SDLC, c'est-à-dire concevoir et livrer du logiciel avec des agents dans la boucle plutôt qu'à côté, demande de faire évoluer tout l'environnement autour : architecture, gestion du contexte, harness (la couche système qui donne à un agent ses outils, ses permissions et son contexte d'exécution), developer platforms, intégration au SI, infrastructure, sécurité, observabilité, évaluation.
Comme Tech Lead, tu aides nos clients à comprendre ces transformations, tu arbitres les décisions d'architecture qui en découlent et tu mets en place les capacités qui leur manquent. Tu conçois, tu conseilles, et tu descends dans le code quand il faut confronter une décision au réel.
Pourquoi on ouvre ce poste
Nos clients ont dépassé le stade du POC. Leur question porte maintenant sur l'intégration des agents au SI et au cycle de delivery, et sur ce qui doit être mutualisé dans une plateforme plutôt que laissé à chaque équipe. Ce sont des questions d'architecture, et on n'a personne dont c'est le métier à plein temps.
Tes missions 🎯
•    comprendre le contexte Product, business et technologique du client, son SI et son environnement de delivery
•    identifier ce que l'IA change et les capacités technologiques qui manquent pour y répondre
•    concevoir les architectures et arbitrer les choix structurants : build ou buy, plateforme ou équipe, standardisation ou autonomie, besoin immédiat ou capacité durable
•    prototyper ou implémenter certains composants quand une décision d'architecture a besoin d'être éprouvée
•    accompagner les équipes client et faire monter les équipes Thiga en compétence
•    intervenir en avant-vente comme garant technique, challenger les demandes et aider le client à transformer un problème flou en décision
Deux exemples de ce que ça donne concrètement 👀
Passer à l'échelle avec les coding agents
Le cas du début. Tu analyses l'existant, tu identifies les capacités manquantes et tu conçois l'architecture qui permet aux équipes et aux agents de travailler ensemble de façon observable et sécurisée. Le vrai sujet est souvent le knowledge : reconstruire un contexte exploitable à partir de repos, de docs et de conventions que personne n'a maintenus depuis trois ans.
Décider ce qui se mutualise
Cinq équipes expérimentent chacune avec leurs propres modèles, agents et outils. Tu aides le client à trancher ce qui remonte dans une plateforme, ce qui reste décentralisé et dans quel ordre y aller. La réponse est rarement la grande plateforme IA. The successful candidate will communicate effectively with team members and internal stakeholders, both verbally and through written content. 

SUMMARY OF RESPONSIBILITIES


Evaluate customer and operational needs to define requirements, integrate technical parameters, and assure compatibility of all physical, functional, and program interfaces.
Represent CesiumAstro in customer meetings, design reviews, and technical discussions across Europe.
Define and validate space system requirements and interfaces, ensuring end-to-end feasibility.
Develop and direct technical concept development in support of proposals and demonstrations.
Participate in developing system engineering processes for requirements management, flow-down, and traceability.
Lead system-level trade studies, including antenna architecture design, modem design, performance analysis and system level integration

Support proposal development, design reviews, and technical documentation. 


JOB REQUIREMENTS AND MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS



M.S. or higher in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related field.
5+ years of experience in system engineering for communications payloads, RF systems, or space/defense platforms.
Very strong background in communication theory.
Practical experience working with antenna systems (design, integration, or performance evaluation).
Experience with and understanding of satellite-communications standards (e.g., NR NTN, DVB-S2x, CCSDS).
Proven ability to capture and manage requirements across multidisciplinary teams.
Excellent communication skills; comfortable presenting to customers and leading design reviews.
Fluent in English (German language skills a plus).
Deep understanding of RF concepts, impairments, and their impacts on system performance.

title: AI Software Engineer (F/H/NB)
description_clean:
SFEIR est un cabinet d'expertise technologique spécialisé dans la conception, l'architecture et l'industrialisation de solutions numériques sur-mesure. Nous accompagnons les organisations dans leurs transformations les plus complexes en combinant la rigueur du Software Craftsmanship avec la maîtrise des technologies d'avenir. Convaincus que la souveraineté numérique est un enjeu stratégique majeur, nous concevons des architectures sécurisées, performantes et indépendantes, portées par des partenariats solides avec des acteurs clés comme SENS et Scaleway. Acteur de référence sur l'intelligence artificielle, nous faisons évoluer les standards d'ingénierie modernes. À travers notre plateforme GenAI RAISE et notre statut de partenaire Anthropic Preferred (au sein du Claude Partner Network), nous plaçons le Context Engineering et l'IA générative au cœur de nos pratiques. 
Nos chiffres clés :


950 consultants passionnés par la tech et augmentés par l’IA.


8 agences en France, au Luxembourg et en Belgique.


Partenaire Anthropic Select au sein du Claude Partner Network.


15 ans de partenariat avec Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, Databricks, Confluent...


+5000 personnes formées par an via le SFEIR Institute.


Rejoindre SFEIR, c'est intégrer un collectif où la culture technique prévaut. Nous offrons des trajectoires de carrière dédiées aux experts (Individual Contributor / IC), te permettant de progresser en haute maîtrise technique sans devoir basculer vers du management organisationnel. Nous intégrons l'IA à nos propres pratiques d'ingénierie (utilisation quotidienne de RAISE et Claude Code) pour automatiser les tâches à faible valeur ajoutée et concentrer nos efforts sur la conception d'architectures résilientes.
▪️ À propos du poste
Tu conçois et déploies des agents IA et systèmes agentiques complets exécutant des processus métier de bout en bout : support client avancé, recherche multi-sources, opérations IT, ainsi que des cas d'usage avancés liés à l'industrie du futur et à la continuité digitale (ex. traçabilité des exigences, maintenance prédictive, continuité de l'ingénierie et jumeaux numériques). Tu sais aussi bien développer des agents sur-mesure en code que configurer des agents via des plateformes low-code/no-code avec des plateformes type Gemini Enterprise.
Ton terrain d'action combine maîtrise technique du cycle de vie logiciel (SDLC) et compréhension fonctionnelle fine des enjeux métiers. Tu orchestres l'autonomie des agents, la planification, le choix des outils et la mémoire, tout en garantissant la fiabilité, la gouvernance et le respect des garde-fous.
Les missions :


Analyser et appréhender les besoins et processus métiers avec une vision fonctionnelle claire pour définir les cas d'usage d'automatisation et la répartition des tâches (autonomie agentique vs validation humaine).


Concevoir et développer des systèmes agentiques complets (mono ou multi-agents), en choisissant l'approche adaptée : développement sur-mesure ou programmation/configuration d'agents low-code/no-code (Gemini Enterprise, Vertex AI Agent Builder, AWS).


Construire les outils des agents : function calling, intégration d’API et de systèmes d’information, création et consommation de serveurs MCP, workflows asynchrones et longue durée.


Maîtriser la fiabilité : gestion des erreurs et des reprises, boucles de contrôle, limites de budget et de pas, comportement face à l’imprévu.


Évaluer les agents : jeux de scénarios, analyse des trajectoires, taux de réussite des tâches, LLM-as-judge, tests de non-régression à chaque changement de prompt, d’outil ou de modèle.


Observer en production : traces détaillées, coûts par tâche, détection des dérives et des boucles, tableaux de bord.


Sécuriser l’autonomie : permissions minimales sur les outils, protection contre la prompt injection, isolation des actions sensibles, validation humaine, traçabilité, conformité (RGPD, AI Act).


S'intégrer dans le cycle de vie logiciel (SDLC) complet et déployer sur le cloud (Google Cloud / Vertex AI) avec intégration CI/CD et gestion des coûts.


Partager : documenter les patterns, former les équipes clientes, contribuer aux publications et événements SFEIR.


▪️ Le profil idéal

5 ans d’expérience en développement logiciel (hors stage et alternance) avec une vision transverse du SDLC et une première expérience solide sur des projets LLM / IA
Pratique démontrée de la création d'agents IA : développement custom (frameworks/code) ou création via des environnements low-code/no-code (Gemini Enterprise, AWS,...)
Connaissance de MCP et des protocoles d’interopérabilité entre agents (A2A)
Compréhension fine des modes d’échec des agents : dérive, boucles, mauvais choix d’outil, perte de contexte
Solide maîtrise des API, de l’asynchrone et des architectures événementielles
Rigueur d’ingénierie : tests, observabilité, code relu
Aisance relationnelle et bon niveau fonctionnel pour échanger avec les équipes métiers, comprendre leurs enjeux et leur expliquer les possibilités et limites des agents IA

Un plus

Expérience d’évaluation d’agents et d’observabilité (OpenTelemetry, Langfuse…)
Connaissance de la méthodologie BMAD 
Google Cloud (Vertex AI, Cloud Run, Gemini),
Sensibilité sécurité : modèles de menaces sur les agents, gestion des identités et des permissions
Notions de RAG, vues comme un outil de l’agent
Contributions open source, side projects agentiques, talks


▪️ L'ancrage Bordelais 
L'agence SFEIR Bordeaux regroupe une quinzaine d'ingénieurs et d'architectes seniors. Tu y trouveras la proximité et l'agilité d'une structure à taille humaine, adossée à la solidité d'un grand groupe. Tu participes activement à l'écosystème tech local (meetups, conférences BDX/IO, SFEIR Talks) et tu peux intégrer le programme AI Champions pour piloter la R&D de l'agence.
▪️ Tes conditions de travail 

Organisation : 2 à 3 jours de télétravail par semaine.
Équipement : Laptop haut de gamme au choix (MacBook Pro ou Dell Precision dernière génération).
Package : Rémunération fixe attractive, prime de vacances, accord d'intéressement, forfait mobilités durables, mutuelle et titres-restaurant.

▪️ Le processus de recrutement 

Échange RH : Alignement sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les opportunités SFEIR.
Session Technique ("PlayOffs") : Évaluation pratique en pair-programming (Algo et GenAI) avec deux Sfeirians.
Échange Métier & Projection : Discussion approfondie sur les cas d'usage, les missions cibles et le contexte client à Bordeaux
Entretien Final : Échange stratégique avec le Directeur d'Agence.

Vestiaire Collective runs a global marketplace on AWS and GCP — Kubernetes, Kafka, Terraform, Vault, Cloudflare, Datadog, a large PHP application under active modernisation, a series of microservices in different tech stacks (Goland, PHP, Node) and a fast-growing surface of AI-powered services. 
 
As Director of Cloud Infrastructure and Security, you will lead a small team of six senior individual contributors across Cloud Infrastructure (DevOps/SRE) and Security. This is a hands-on Director role: alongside setting the strategy and roadmap, you will work directly with the team on architecture, technical decisions, incidents and delivery. What you will do:
Leadership across two teams


Directly lead, develop and retain a small team of six (6) experienced engineers across Cloud Infrastructure and Security. This is a player-coach role without multiple management layers, so you will remain close to the team’s technical work and day-to-day priorities.

Consolidate observability into a single source of truth for metrics, logs and traces.


Improve developer experience and delivery throughput: CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions), paved roads, test environments on demand, and delivery metrics that hold up.


Own FinOps: infrastructure cost per unit of business value, cost accountability pushed back to each team, and continued run-rate reduction. Cost discipline is a first-class objective.


Support the modernisation of our core platform: Tech migrations, runtime and framework upgrades, and continuous database and Kubernetes upgrades.


Attack toil systematically: automate the recurring requests, and hand safe self-service back to product teams rather than absorbing the work.


Grow the foundations for AI-augmented engineering and operations


Security

Strengthen cloud security posture management (CNAPP) and secure-by-default configurations across all environments.


Improve Embedding security into the SDLC and CI/CD: establish full static-analysis and dependency-scanning coverage with clear criteria for when critical findings block a release.


Mature vulnerability management, penetration testing and our bug bounty program into one prioritised program with SLAs and aging reports that measurably reduce risk.


Advance identity and access management toward least privilege and zero trust: automated provisioning from groups, and periodic access reviews.


Mature logging, detection and incident response, closing SIEM coverage gaps

Keep security awareness and training relevant to a threat landscape that now includes AI-enabled social engineering.


Who you are:


8+ years with a Significant experience in Infrastructure, Platform Engineering, DevOps, SRE or Cloud Security, including experience leading engineers.


You may currently be an Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager or Head of who is ready to broaden your scope and step into a first Director role.

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-Doctoral Position Ferroelectric-Based Ternary Computing: From Circuit Design to System-Level Integration Scientific Context
description_clean: Energy efficiency remains one of the foremost challenges in modern computing, spanning from edge IoT devices to high-performance data centers. Conventional CMOS-based architectures are approaching fundamental physical limits, while the "memory wall" — data transfers between processor and memory accounting for 70 to 90% of total system energy — continues to worsen with the ever-growing demands of data-intensive workloads such as deep neural networks and signal processing pipelines.In-Memory Computing (IMC) has emerged as a disruptive paradigm to overcome these bottlenecks by embedding arithmetic operations directly within memory arrays, drastically reducing data movement. In this landscape, ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) stand out as particularly compelling devices: fully compatible with standard CMOS fabrication processes, non-volatile, reconfigurable, and capable of storing intermediate polarization states — a property that naturally enables ternary logic within a single device.The Post-Doctoral position will cover at least one of the following tasks:Design Standard Cell Technology Library based on FeFET devices developed at INL in order to be used with synthesis flow.Design and optimize ternary arithmetic units (multiply-accumulate units, adders, comparators) based on the FeFET ternary gate library developed within the project, targeting area, power, and timing closure under realistic process constraints.Develop and refine system-level models of FeFET-based ternary IMC units, abstracting circuit-level characterization results into architecture simulators, enabling design space exploration across the full heterogeneous system.Investigate hardware/software co-design strategies for mapping real-world applications — particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and signal processing kernels — onto the ternary IMC fabric, exploiting approximate computing techniques to trade precision for energy efficiency.Assess and benchmark the energy, performance, and accuracy trade-offs of ternary IMC against binary CMOS and binary NVM-based IMC reference implementations, using both synthetic benchmarks and real application workloads.Contribute to the definition of a design methodology for ternary ferroelectric circuits, including EDA tool flows, cell library characterization guidelines, and design rules, with the aim of enabling broader community adoption.  Required Candidate ProfileThe ideal candidate holds a PhD in microelectronics, computer architecture, or a closely related field, and demonstrates at least one of the following hard skills:Circuit and architecture design: Strong expertise in digital circuit design flows and computer architecture, with hands-on experience using industrial EDA tools (Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Synopsys). Experience with standard-cell library characterization is a plus.Emerging memory technologies: Solid knowledge of non-volatile memory devices, preferably including ferroelectric materials (FeFET, FeCap) or resistive memories (RRAM, PCM). Familiarity with compact modeling is an asset.System-level design and simulation: Experience with architecture-level simulation frameworks and hardware/software co-design methodologies. Knowledge of RISC-V ecosystems is a plus.Application domains: Familiarity with deep neural network inference workloads and/or digital signal processing pipelines, particularly in the context of approximate or energy-constrained computing.Programming: Proficiency in HDL (Verilog, VHDL, Verilog-A) and scripting languages (Python, Shell) for design automation and simulation.Soft skills: Scientific leadership, ability to coordinate with PhD students and international partners, strong publication record consistent with career stage, and excellent written and oral communication in English.Language: Fluent scientific English is mandatory. title: Senior Product Manager (Giftcard)
description_clean:
Atolls is the world's largest community-driven shopping platform, active in 20+ markets. 
We help millions make smarter spending decisions across discovery, evaluation, and (re-)purchase by connecting people with the right brands and retailers.
Our 1,000+ team across 10 countries builds products used every day at global scale, where you'll have real ownership and see your impact. Want to shape the destinations people rely on to shop with confidence? Keep reading.

About This Role:
We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to take ownership of our Gift Cards vertical - one of the fastest-growing parts of our alternative offers, spanning gift card purchase, redemption, provider partnerships, and cross-market growth across UK, Germany, and Spain.
This is a high-ownership, high-visibility role. You'll set the strategy for a business line generating triple-digit YoY growth in some markets, own the commercial relationships with our gift card providers, and work directly with our Fulfilment leadership on where the vertical goes next. You'll also work closely with - and may grow into ownership of - adjacent parts of our Alternative Offers and in-store rewards portfolio.
We want a strong senior product leader: someone who has built and scaled products at a leading tech company and/or a startup, who thinks and acts like an entrepreneur, and who can move a commercial product forward with minimal hand-holding.

Our Benefits:
At Atolls, we believe in nurturing both your professional and personal growth. Here's what you can expect:

A culture that values personal and professional development, with internal mobility opportunities.
A supportive and open-minded team that embraces diverse perspectives and innovative ideas.
32 days of paid vacation plus your birthday off, giving you the time you need to recharge.
A flexible hybrid working scheme to balance work and life.
Access to a learning budget and internal training to help you grow in your role.
Mental health coaching to support your well-being.
Regular global and local get-togethers to celebrate successes and build connections.
The possibility of taking a sabbatical after three years with the company.
A cloud-based company setup, providing flexibility and collaboration opportunities no matter where you are.

*These are global benefits that apply to all employees, with additional local perks based on your location.

Responsibilities:
In this role, you will:

Own the gift card product strategy and roadmap - from provider selection and inventory quality to the end-to-end purchase, redemption, and admin experience.
Lead commercial and provider negotiations - framework agreements, commission structures, SLAs, and multi-entity contracting with gift card providers (e.g. Finperks, Tillo), in partnership with Operations, Legal and Finance.
Drive revenue growth across markets - set and deliver GMV and commission targets across France, Germany, and Spain, backed by rigorous transaction-level analysis.
Partner cross-functionally - work daily with engineering, design, data, CRM, and adjacent product teams to ship a coherent gift card experience across web, app, and browser extension.
Use data to lead, not just report - build and refine models (e.g. fraud-tier scoring), validate revenue and performance data with Finance, and identify the next highest-impact bet.
Represent the vertical at the leadership level - bring clear recommendations and trade-offs to cross-team and leadership forums, and help shape Alternative Offers' broader strategic direction.
Build for scale - help expand gift cards from a standalone catalogue page into a fully integrated offer type across the platform.


 Your Profile:

5+ years in product management, including significant time owning a product or business line end-to-end at a leading tech company and/or a startup.
A strong entrepreneurial track record - you've built something from close to zero, made judgment calls with imperfect data, and taken ownership beyond your formal remit.
Commercial fluency - comfortable owning revenue targets, running vendor/partner negotiations, and thinking in margin, commission, and unit economics, not just features.
Strong analytical skills - fluent working with transaction and revenue data to make and defend decisions; comfortable partnering with data/finance teams on models like fraud scoring.
Proven cross-functional leadership - experience leading engineering, design, and data counterparts in a fast-paced, matrixed environment, without formal authority over them.
Excellent stakeholder management - able to influence and present confidently to senior/executive stakeholders.
A degree from a top-tier university (e.g. Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, HEC Paris, ESSEC, Sciences Po, Bocconi, ETH Zurich, or equivalent); an MBA or further qualification from a leading program is a plus.
Fluent English required


Our hiring process:

TA Call: Meet one of our Talent Experts and get to know Atolls better.
Technical Round: Focus on the technical aspects of the role (Through a Live Case), and meet your potential manager.
Final Round: Meet other Atollians 🏝️It varies from 1 to 3 interviews

*Some processes might slightly change according to needs

Ready to apply?
Be part of a destination where your work helps millions of people make better decisions every day. One focused application is all we need. If you truly fit more than one role, you're welcome to apply to up to three. This helps us match you with the right opportunity faster.We review every application with equal care and will reach out if your profile aligns. Apply now with your CV in English.*Portfolios, writing samples, or certifications may be requested based on the role.#LI-PM1


At Atolls, we want to ensure that all employees can thrive in an inclusive environment. Our employment opportunities are open to every gender, race, religion, age, sexual orientation, ability, place of origin, or socioeconomic status. We remain committed to a culture of diversity, equity and belonging, where all employees are welcomed, respected, connected, and engaged. 

As part of our recruitment process at Atolls, we use AI tools for interview recording and transcription. These tools are designed to assist our teams and are never used independently to make hiring decisions. Every assessment and hiring decision is made by our hiring panel and team through human judgment.Before your first interview, you will receive an email with the option to opt out. You can also change your preference at any time during the recruitment process by using the link in that email or by contacting your Talent Acquisition Partner.
The use of AI, or the choice not to use it, will not affect your application in any way.

title: Product Manager
description_clean: OUR MISSIONTo become the car-changing destination of choice. By combining technology, media and deep automotive expertise, we've turned how people buy, sell, advertise and lease cars on its head.What started as a simple reviews site is now one of the largest online car-changing destinations in Europe. Last year alone we grew over 50% with nearly £3bn worth of cars bought on site, while £1.8bn of cars were listed for sale through our Sell My Car service.In 2024 we went big and acquired Autovia - creators of AutoExpress and Evo magazines - doubling our audience overnight. Together we now have one of the biggest YouTube channels in the world with almost 10m subscribers and over 1.1 billion annual views, while we sell 1.2 million print copies of our magazines and have an annual web content reach over 350million.And we’re a long way from done!THE ROLEBuying and selling a car should feel like one seamless motion for a dealer, not two separate systems. Right now it's the opposite: a dealer buys through us, then has to manage collection, payment and resale largely on their own, stitching together workflows across multiple platforms and channels, much of it manual.For a dealer, speed is money. Every extra day a car sits before it's collected, priced, and paid for is a day of depreciation, tied-up capital, and a missed chance to buy the next one.If we can get a dealer from 'I've bought this car' to 'it's ready and paid for' faster through transport and collections, quicker final pricing, and Wallet, we make them more profitable. A dealer who's more profitable because of Carwow has little reason to go elsewhere: they'll lean on us more, and churn less.This role owns that last-mile agenda: getting cars collected quickly, resolving final price without friction, and making Wallet work the way dealers expect it to. This team sits across our ambitions to make car changing a seamless journey, this role's job is the handover itself: the operational moment between buying and being ready to sell again. This is also a moment where AI changes what's possible. Dealers are already asking for smarter scheduling, less manual chasing, and tools that reduce the overhead of running a business. We want to build those things. The PM in this role will need the curiosity to explore what that could look like, and the rigour to distinguish genuine value from noise. If you want to own an operational product area end to end, work with some of the most sophisticated buyers in UK retail, and build things that have a direct line to commercial outcomes, this is it. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOINGProduct Strategy & Execution: Own the product direction for Carwow's dealer-facing product, defining what we build, in what order, and whyLead discovery work with dealers, interviews, on-site visits, data analysis to build a precise understanding of where we can add the most valueIdentify and test opportunities to bring AI into dealer workflows: smarter recommendations, vehicle pricing, performance insights that actually change behaviourCollaborate with Tech Lead, Designer, and Engineers to ship well-scoped solutions with clear success metricsManage the backlog with commercial awareness prioritising work that drives engagement, retention, and revenue, not just activityPartner Engagement & Insight:Build relationships with key dealer partners and use those relationships to validate product direction before we buildWork with Account Management and Sales to understand what's driving churn, what's blocking adoption, and what would make carwow stickierTranslate qualitative partner feedback into structured product insight; don't just collect opinions, turn them into decisionsCross-functional Leadership:Work across product, engineering, commercial, and marketing to align on priorities and ship coherentlyCommunicate strategy and trade-offs clearly to leadership and stakeholders, written as well as verbalSupport the commercial team on partner conversations where product context matters: capability deep-dives, roadmap discussions, strategic accountsWHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR1.5+ years of product management experience in a B2B or SaaS environment, with evidence of improving engagement or retention metricsHands-on experience with product discovery: you run your own interviews, interrogate your own data, and form your own hypotheses rather than waiting for research to land in your inboxGenuine curiosity about AI,  you follow what's happening, you have a point of view on where it adds real value, and you're eager to experimentComfort with ambiguity: this role involves defining the problem as much as solving it, and the scope will evolveStrong stakeholder instincts, you can build trust with commercial teams, technical partners, and senior stakeholders without losing your own point of viewClear written and verbal communication; description_clean:
Who We Are
At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing.
Why Join Us
We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.Job Overview
We are at a pivotal point in our tech progression. We're looking to grow our technical estate, architect new systems, remove technical debt and scale our platform. It's an exciting time to join Partnerize, and we are looking for a technical leader to help spearhead this evolution.
As a database engineer, you will operate with a high degree of autonomy, acting as the principal technical authority and taking end-to-end ownership of our database estate. You will be a strategic anchor within the Technical Operations team, interfacing directly with business, development, and IT functions. While you will own the database architecture and design solutions for the future, a fundamental, non-negotiable part of this role is hands-on Business As Usual incident management. You must be comfortable rolling up your sleeves to handle daily operations, backups, and performance tuning alongside project delivery.
Your deep expertise in MySQL, alongside strong Linux system administration and a working knowledge of network troubleshooting, will be critical to your success. You will design, build, and secure the underlying servers our databases run on, proactively analyse current implementations, and act as the ultimate technical escalation point for our database infrastructure in both our physical datacenters as well as our public cloud estate.
While we need your advanced technical skills, we are equally focused on character. We are looking for a highly proactive communicator who collaborates seamlessly without needing to be prompted. Crucially, you must be able to independently plan out complex technical work, such as database upgrades, and clearly articulate the step-by-step process and business impacts to stakeholders. You must thrive both when working independently to tackle complex problems and when operating collaboratively within a broader team. Furthermore, you will actively seek out opportunities to coach and mentor other engineers, elevating the overall DBA knowledge across the company. This role is fully remote and open to candidates based anywhere in the UK or the US.
As a Database Engineer at Partnerize, You Will:

Primary Operational Ownership: Take complete, hands-on ownership of daily database operations. Managing and maintaining the database infrastructure for day-to-day use, including backup management, resolving slow-running queries, and performance tuning, is a fundamental pillar of this role.
Infrastructure & Server Support: Be comfortable in providing operational support by designing, securing, and robustly maintaining the underlying Linux servers that our large distributed databases run on.
Project Planning & Stakeholder Communication: Plan, manage, and deliver large technical projects like database upgrades and migrations. You will autonomously map out step-by-step execution plans, proactively communicate technical considerations, and clearly articulate the business impact of your work to non-technical stakeholders.
Technical Leadership & Strategy: Scope incoming work, delegate to team members where appropriate, and act as the definitive database escalation point for support teams within the wider organisation.
Proactive Optimisation & Automation: Measure and optimise system performance to push our capabilities forward. Lead the automation of management and monitoring for the database platform infrastructure.
Collaboration & Documentation: Partner closely with development teams, product owners, and other stakeholders to ensure database needs are met and to improve the testability of database aspects within software deployments. Document procedures, best practices, and troubleshooting steps for knowledge sharing.
Delivery & Out-of-Hours/On-Call Support: Plan, prioritise, and estimate tasks using Jira, and provide essential support for any critical database-related issues both during and outside of normal business hours.
Mentorship: Actively mentor and coach other engineers, providing technical leadership on database design, optimisation, and migration strategies to elevate overall team knowledge.

Essential Knowledge, Skills and Experience

MySQL & On-Premise Infrastructure: Advanced administration of MySQL in production environments, whether on-premise or in the cloud. Crucially, as our primary database is on-premise, you must possess strong Linux system administration and networking awareness to independently support, secure, and maintain the underlying servers.
Independence: Experience as either the sole or lead owner for large production database infrastructure within a SaaS environment with demonstrable accountability for its availability and performance. A proven track record of managing these responsibilities while coordinating with external technical stakeholders and adhering to light change management processes.
High Availability & Replication: Advanced experience configuring and troubleshooting complex MySQL replication setups (such as primary-replica, multi-master, and GTID). Proven ability to quickly resolve replication lag, manage smooth failovers, and execute disaster recovery plans. 
Monitoring: A working understanding of database monitoring tools and patterns. What to measure, appropriate thresholds, and response mechanics.
Performance Optimisation: Deep expertise in query tuning, slow query analysis, and advanced schema optimisation (including normalisation, partitioning, query rewrites, and indexing strategies).
Upgrades, Migrations & Scripting: Proven track record of executing minimal-downtime upgrades and complex migrations (in-place, cross-database, or migrating ancillary workloads). Highly skilled in automating these processes using Python and/or Bash to build robust, version-controlled scripts.
Database Security & Compliance: Experience securing database infrastructure through SSL/TLS encryption, user access control, audit logging, and automated backup encryption.

Desirable Knowledge, Skills and Experience

Automation, Containers & CI/CD: Hands-on expertise using Ansible for configuration management, deploying and managing databases within Kubernetes/containerised environments, and managing version control and pipelines via GitLab for any database related change.
Monitoring & Troubleshooting: Hands-on experience deploying and configuring monitoring/alerting stacks (such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Percona Monitoring and Management) for proactive issue resolution and database health tracking.
PostgreSQL & Hybrid Estates: Advanced administration of PostgreSQL, alongside experience managing database workloads across a hybrid environment (e.g., combining on-premise architecture with AWS).
OLAP & Data Warehousing (Apache Druid / Snowflake): Familiarity with columnar databases and cloud data platforms, particularly Apache Druid and Snowflake. Experience with schema design, data sharding strategies, OLAP query optimisation for long-running queries, and managing zero-downtime upgrades in distributed environments.
Service Management Tooling: Experience using Jira and Confluence for managing workflows, project tracking, and creating technical documentation.

Growth & Innovation:


Openness to learn the required technologies.
An interest in development, new technologies and innovation.
Supporting development teams into the refactoring of technical debt.


At Partnerize, we recognise it is unrealistic for a candidate to fulfil 100% of the criteria in this job description. We encourage you to apply if you feel you meet the majority of the requirements above. We know that skills evolve over time, so if you have a keen appetite to learn and evolve alongside us over time, come join our team!

We strive to foster an environment where people can be their authentic selves, raise concerns and innovate, all without fear; where they are treated fairly and respectfully, have equal access to opportunities and resources and can contribute fully to the organization's success. lead the legal plan for migrating customers from Swan (sequencing, consent/novation approaches, customer communications from a legal standpoint, continuity of mandates, handling of incidents/complaints, and safeguards to minimise conduct risk).Privacy and Security In close coordination with our DPO (Léa) and security stakeholders, you ensure that our Financial Services operating
